title: Rollback choreography and customer liaison runbook for interleaved hosted/dedicated/private model regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Runbook and orchestration plan for handling model rollout regressions that span Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. Focus is on coordinated mitigation (pin/pause/rollback), customer-facing communications, and a reproducible choreography for engineers and CSMs to follow when a model variant causes high-severity regressions during or immediately after canary rollouts.
goals: Provide a single, unambiguous incident flow for regressions that affect multiple deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
Minimize customer downtime and trust impact via fast mitigation + clear comms.
Reduce decision latency by defining roles, authority boundaries, and safe rollback/pin actions for each environment.
Preserve forensic signal (logs, tokens, cached KV state) required for root cause analysis without blocking urgent mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: On-call can enact the runbook from Slack/Playbook within 15 minutes of P0 being declared.
Runbook includes validated commands for pinning to prior model variant across hosted/dedicated/private with expected latencies documented.
Customer-facing templates exist and are approved by Legal and CSM for P0/P1 escalation lanes.
Post-incident checklist captures artifacts for RCA: Grafana links, model diffs, prompt repros, and affected customer list.
runbook_steps: 1) Initial triage (0-5 min): IC checks alert source and affected surfaces (generation, embeddings, reranking). Post initial note in #prod-incidents with tags #customer-impact and environment tags (hosted/dedicated/private).
2) Declare severity (5-10 min): Use standardized severity rubric. If incorrect outputs affect >1 customer or SLAs, declare P0 and page SRE + runtime + model-owner + CSM.

3) Stop further rollout (10-15 min): If a canary is running, immediately pause rollout in orchestration console (rollout->pause). For automated rollouts, flip canary gating to manual. Communicate in Slack channel the exact model version being paused.

4) Mitigation decision tree (15-30 min): Check fast mitigations in order: (A) Pin to previous verified model variant (hosted) using rollback API; (B) For Dedicated, failover traffic to reserved GPU pool running verified variant; (C) For Private customers, coordinate with customer SRE for local pin or instruct them to revert agent via signed package and provide commands. Document decision in incident channel and update ticket.

5) Short-term customer path (15-40 min): If customer-visible regression, CSM posts initial templated message (see templates) and offers ETA window. Engineering confirms mitigation ETA and expected user experience after mitigation.

6) Execute mitigation (30-60 min): Runtime engineer runs verified commands: example 'redwoodctl model pin --customer <id> --model <ver>' for hosted; trigger dedicated pool swap for reserved capacity; provide signed rollback package and step-by-step for private. Do NOT flush KV cache unless instructed by model owner; if cache invalidation is required, schedule it with a 5-min notice in incident channel.

7) Validate (60-90 min): Run regression smoke prompts from the customer repro set against the pinned variant. Capture token-level logs and compare against failure traces. If mitigation succeeds, mark incident as stabilized and proceed to communications (customer update + incident summary).

8) If mitigation fails (90+ min): Escalate to on-call engineering lead and consider a hotpatch rollout (binary patch) vs full rollback depending on root cause. If cross-region capacity is available, route traffic to fallback region with compatible model variant and document traffic split percentage used.

9) Post-incident (24-72 hrs): Complete RCA with model diff, perf profiles, kernel/quantization traces, and CS impact table. Schedule a customer readout for impacted enterprise customers. Create follow-ups for tooling gaps identified during the incident.
communication_templates: Internal (Slack) — initial: "P0 declared: model regression affecting generation quality for customers X,Y,Z. Candidate mitigation: pin hosted->v1.24, swap dedicated to pool-id=us-west-2-reserve, coordinate with private customer ops for revert. IC: @<name>"

Customer initial (CS template): "We’re actively investigating an issue affecting model outputs and have prioritized a mitigation that should restore expected behavior. We’ll share an update within 60 minutes. If you can, please provide a short set of inputs that reproduce the issue. — Redwood Support"

Customer follow-up (mitigated): "Update: We reverted to the previous verified model variant at <time> which restores expected behavior. We’re running an internal postmortem and will schedule a technical readout. Contact <CSM> for account-specific questions."
Public-facing status (status.redwood.com): "Degraded: model inference latency/quality issue impacting a subset of hosted customers. Mitigation in progress. Estimated recovery within 2 hours."
escalation_matrix: Severity P0: Page SRE (PagerDuty P0), runtime lead, model owner, CSM. Exec notice to be prepared within 30 min. IC owns timeline and customer comms.
Severity P1: Notify runtime on-call and model owner. CSM triages customer list and consolidates comms. Target response within 60 min.
Severity P2/P3: Triage in regular on-call flow, track in weekly ops review. No immediate pages unless impact escalates.
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Chose 'pin-first' strategy for hosted rollouts because it preserves KV cache and reduces cold-start risk compared to full binary rollback. Agreed by runtime and model teams.
2026-02-18: Decided to require explicit customer consent before automated rollback on Private deployments. Security/Legal review flagged data residency concerns for automatic packages.
2026-03-05: Feedback from CSMs: initial templates were too technical. Updated customer templates to include simple impact/ETA language and CS-nominated contact. Approved by Legal on 2026-03-07.

notes_for_oncall: Always attach the model artifact digest (sha256) and rollout id to the incident ticket before any pin/rollback action.
If customer is Dedicated or Private, contact assigned CSM before executing any disruptive action (unless explicitly authorized in SLA).
Avoid simultaneous KV flush and model swap for hosted customers; prefer pin then controlled cache invalidation after verification.
